messages:
mia: quick sanity check — I just ran a tiny bring-up for the new reranker on quantized-INT8 checkpoints. seeing weird NDCG delta when docs are padded vs truncated. can someone eyeball the setup?

sanjay: can you paste the eval command + a couple of lines of the output? also which dataset split and tokenization? :thinking_face:

mia: running on small holdout (50 queries) from prod-like sample. tokenization = tiktoken-compat, model = rwrk-bert-xxl-int8 (converted via ptq). command: `./eval_rerank --model rwrk-bert-xxl-int8 --qfile queries.jsonl --docs docs.jsonl --trunc-doc 512 --pad-doc 512 --metric ndcg@10,mrr`

mia: output snippet:
```
N=50
ndcg@10: baseline_fp32=0.412, quant_int8=0.395, delta=-0.017
mrr: baseline_fp32=0.531, quant_int8=0.526, delta=-0.005
note: when trunc-doc=256 (no padding) ndcg delta = -0.004
```

omar: interesting — two quick hypotheses: (1) padding-to-512 is introducing positional/context differences for our reranker architecture (it expects left-aligned doc tokens). (2) truncation at 256 accidentally removes late relevance signals for long docs, changing ranking ordering and variance.

rachel: also check whether your doc separators or sentinel tokens are being added before or after padding. small mismatch between training preprocessing and eval (e.g., [DOC_SEP] placement) can flip ndcg a few points.

mia: good call. training used `doc + [SEP] + metadata` then padded. eval used `pad then add [SEP]` (oops). will re-run with consistent ordering.

sanjay: aside: the sample size (50 queries) is tiny — stochastic noise will hide true regressed quality. run at least 1k queries or bootstrap to get CIs. Also compute pairwise significance (bootstrap) and per-query delta distribution rather than only averages.

mia: noted. re-run plan: 1) fix sep placement, 2) run 1k queries, 3) bucket by query length and doc length, 4) compare ndcg@10 + mrr + per-query delta CCDF.

eval-bot: automated-run: eval_id=run-1900112223-1 
status: queued -> running

omar: another gotcha — quantized kernels may change softmax/score numeric stability when logits are small; for rerankers small score perturbations reorder ties. consider calibrating score scaling or using fp16 scorer pass for final scoring if latency allows.

rachel: for dataset selection: make sure holdout reflects recency and long-tail doc lengths. add a small adversarial slice (docs with boilerplate headers, long code blocks) — those often behave differently under quantization/padding.

mia: re-run finished (quick local smoke):
```
N=1000
ndcg@10: baseline_fp32=0.418, quant_int8=0.414, delta=-0.004 (p=0.12 bootstrap)
mrr: baseline_fp32=0.536, quant_int8=0.532, delta=-0.004 (p=0.21)
per-query: 72% queries have abs(delta) < 0.01, tail shows 5% with >0.05 loss
```

mia: conclusion so far: most of the delta was preprocessing mismatch + sample noise. quantization adds small additional variance (tail). next steps: run Dedicated eval across 5 seeds, add score-scaling ablation, and produce a charts PR for the reranker onboarding doc.

sanjay: agree. add regression alerts on per-slice NDCG (long-docs, code-heavy, short-queries) in the eval dashboard.

omar: if tail is business-critical, we can try symmetric quantization or per-channel scales for the final linear layer; also consider KV-cache-friendly quant options if we move to larger context.

rachel: I'll draft a short checklist for onboarding new rerank models: preprocess parity check, tokenization & sep placement, padding/trunc rules, sample size >=1k, bucketed metrics, bootstrap p-values, and example artifacts (diff histograms + CCDF).

mia: perfect — thanks all. I'll open the eval run artifacts and a PR with the charts. :rocket:
